sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they were referred before the Tribunal.

The petitioner filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- on account of injuries received by him in the accident that was occurred on 02.08.2010 in which the offending bus belonging to APSRTC bearing Registration No.AP 28 Z 2042 was involved.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 02.08.2010 while the petitioner was on duty as one of the drivers of the offending bus, he was assisting the other driver of the bus, while it was reversing.
In the said process, the other driver of the bus/respondent No.2, drove the bus in rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner.
As a result of which the petitioner fell down and the bus wheels ran over the right leg of the petitioner thereby he sustained severe crush injuries.
The petitioner was shifted to SVS Medical College, Eanugonda, Mahaboobnagar District for treatment and later he was shifted to Image Hospital, Hyderabad for better treatment.
In this hospital, he underwent treatment as in patient from 03.08.2010 to 26.08.2010 and again from 01.09.2010 to 12.10.2010.
He was again admitted in Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad on 06.11.2010 and was discharged on 22.12.2010.
In view of the crush injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability and did not attend the duty for 35 months, thereby he lost salary of Rs.6,34,319/-.
4. It is further case of the petitioner that he requires Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment for lengthening of his leg.
He was examined by the Medical Board which certified that the petitioner is unfit to be a driver and recommended to provide alternative employment, in as much as his leg was shortened by 3 inches.
5. A case in Cr.No.211 of 2010 was registered against respondent No.2 under Section 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
In view of the crush injuries received by him, he approached the Tribunal, by filing claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- together with interest.

6. The respondents resisted the claim of the petitioner by filing counter affidavit, contending that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner in as much as he has not guided the respondent No.2 properly, while the bus was reversing.
It was further contended that the entire medical expenses incurred by the petitioner were paid by the respondents and he was also provided alternative employment.

It was further contended that the salary was paid for leave period and the petitioner did not submit the information with regard to the accident to the respondent No.1 and he has to prove disability and loss of income.
7. With the above pleadings, the respondents prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
8. In order to prove the case of the petitioner he has examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
Apart from the same, Exs.
C1 to C5 and Exs.X1 to X3 were marked through his witnesses.

On the other hand, the respondents have exhibited attested copy of the payment order of medical Apsrtc vs Dhrakshna Chandra Mouli on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131684606/
3 expenditure of the petitioner and marked the same as Ex.B1.
No witnesses were examined on behalf of the respondents.

9. Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before the Tribunal, the claim petition filed by the petitioner was partly allowed by awarding the amount of Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation together with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim till the date of realization.
Aggrieved by this, the present appeal is filed.
10. The petitioner filed Cross Objections stating that he did not receive the salary from 03.08.2010 to 05.08.2013, and he is entitled to receive the same.

11. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondents/cross objector.
12.
Perused the record.
13. The appeal is filed questioning the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and there was no negligence on the part of respondent No.2/driver of APSRTC.

To substantiate the grounds raised in the present appeal, the respondents/APSRTC neither adduced any oral evidence nor marked any documentary evidence, except marking bald and vague allegations in the counter affidavit, nothing is elicited before the Tribunal to show that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner/claimant.

13. On the other hand, the petitioner has filed the copies of F.I.R and Charge Sheet which were marked as Exhibits A1 and A3 to show that the accident was occurred in view of the negligence of the driver/respondent No.2 of the offending bus.
14. On perusal of the contents of the said documents, it would show that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of respondent No.2.
In the absence of any evidence on behalf of the respondents, the contention of the respondents cannot be believed and accordingly, the same is rejected.

15. Coming to the quantum awarded by the Tribunal is concerned; the petitioner has marked the wound certificate and disability certificate as Exhibits A2 and A4 which would show that the petitioner received crush injuries in the accident that was occurred due to the negligence of respondent No.2.
16.
Apart from the same, the petitioner also got marked Exs. C1 to C5; through the Doctors who treated him.
On examination of the documentary evidence put forth by the petitioner, it is succinctly clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries.
As already noted supra, the respondents have not placed anything on record to disprove the same.
Taking into consideration of the exhibits placed before the Tribunal, it has awarded an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation together with interest at 9% p.a.

For the reasons recorded supra, this Court does not find any illegality or infirmity in the order passed by the Tribunal in so far as the compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner is concerned.

4 17.
Be that as it may, the petitioner filed Cross Objections on the ground that he did not receive the salary from 03.08.2010 to 05.08.2013.
This statement/contention raised by the petitioner was not disputed by the respondents.

Further, on perusal of evidence of PW.5 - Depot Manager,
Dharmavaram, it is clear that she has admitted that no salary was paid to the petitioner during the said period except payment of amount of Rs.1,15,382/.
Further, she admitted that the petitioner is entitled to receive an amount of Rs.5,99,782/- towards salary for the above said period.

18. Despite the fact that the Depot Manager, Dharmavaram admitting that the respondents are liable to pay an amount of Rs.5,99,782/- towards the salary, the Tribunal lost sight of the same, and did not take into consideration while awarding compensation.

19. As there is no dispute with regard to the entitlement of the petitioner for Rs.5,99,782/- in as much as the same has been admitted by PW.5 - Depot Manager, Dharmavaram, this Court is inclined to allow the Cross Objections by directing the respondents to pay a sum of Rs.5,99,782/-
together with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
20. Accordingly, MACMA No.108 of 2019 is dismissed and Cross Objections No.9/2019 is allowed as indicated as above.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending applications, if any shall stand closed.
JUSTICE T.C.D. SEKHAR Date: 05.03.2026.
